docs.article:
Monitor production#

Four signals tell you whether a Verse deployment is healthy, and every one of them is plain HTTP — no agent to install, no credential needed for the uptime check. All calls below were run against a live server.

1. Uptime: GET /v1/health/deep#

No auth (a monitor must not need a credential to ask "are you down?"), rate-limited, and cheap by contract: in-memory counters plus a touch-and-unlink probe on the volume — never a compile. 200 when every check passes, 503 otherwise, so a dumb uptime monitor can alarm on status alone and a smart one can read which subsystem broke:

Code
curl -sS -D - https://HOST/v1/health/deep
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK
# {"ok":true,"checks":{
#    "volumeWritable":true,            touch+unlink in ingest/
#    "compilerPresent":true,           verse-compile binary present
#    "signingKey":true,                Ed25519 key loaded at boot
#    "disk":{"freeMB":491739,"totalMB":948534,"usedPct":48},   ok:false below 512 MB free
#    "storage":{"backend":"s3","bucket":"…","reachable":true}, only with VERSE_STORAGE=s3; unreachable bucket = 503
#    "lastIngest":{"t":1790833829990,"ok":true},               null before the first upload
#    "ingestLastHour":{"attempts":18,"done":16,"failed":2},
#    "telemetryWritable":true}}

Point your uptime service at it with a 1–5 minute interval. Also keep the cheap GET / (the platform health check Railway uses).

2. Ingest health: GET /v1/ops/ingest-stats#

Account auth required (any valid account token or the /studio cookie). The last 24 hours of compile outcomes from the server's persisted ring of the last 200 ingests, plus the client-side failures the server never saw:

Code
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/ops/ingest-stats -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN"
# {"last24h":{"attempts":68,"done":61,"failed":7,
#             "byReason":{"failed":7,"evicted":46},"p50s":5,"p95s":19},
#  "recent":[{"t":…,"idHash":"ace65061d8ab","sizeMB":77.32,"outcome":"done","seconds":613}, …],
#  "telemetry24h":{"canaryFails":0,"uploadFails":1,"loadErrors":0,
#                  "lastCanaryFail":null,"lastUploadFail":{"t":…,"detail":"HTTP 400: …","phase":"upload"}}}

What to watch:

FieldHealthyWorry when
byReason.safe-mode-usedabsent or rarerising — compiles are landing only via the low-memory retry; the box is starved before hard OOMs begin
byReason.timeout / oom0any — look at recent[].sizeMB: a tiny file timing out means CPU starvation, a huge one means a real limit
byReason.storage-full0any — uploads are being refused with 507; raise the volume or VERSE_VPK_BUDGET_MB
byReason.evictedhousekeepingfine on its own (unowned scenes reclaimed by the disk budget), but owners should claim scenes they care about
p95stens of seconds for products, minutes for scansclimbing week over week on similar sizes
telemetry24h.uploadFails with phase: "upload"0the edge answered uploads itself (a bare 400/502 without X-Verse-Error) — the app never saw them; this is the only place they show

Scene ids are stored hashed (idHash); raw ids never enter the log.

3. The canary#

A probe uploads a tiny fixture every 15 minutes with X-Verse-Name: canary, polls it to done, fetches the compiled .vpk, and on any failure POSTs a { "kind": "canary-fail", "detail": "<class>" } telemetry row. ingest-stats.telemetry24h.canaryFails counts them, lastCanaryFail carries the detail, and /studio surfaces the most recent one. Canary artifacts older than 24 h are pruned by the sweeper.

On the reference deployment the probe is web/test/qa-smoke-remote.mjs, run by the verse-worker service against the public URL (so a green canary also proves the compile-fleet path); set VERSE_ALERT_WEBHOOK on that service for Slack-compatible alerts. The same script is the post-deploy smoke:

Code
node web/test/qa-smoke-remote.mjs https://HOST            # 9 checks, ~2 s; exit 1 on any failure
node web/test/qa-smoke-remote.mjs https://HOST --no-ingest --json   # read-only
node web/test/qa-smoke-remote.mjs https://HOST --report --webhook https://hooks.slack.com/…  # canary mode

Or run a minimal one from any cron box:

Code
#!/bin/sh
BASE=https://HOST
fail() { curl -sS -o /dev/null -X POST "$BASE/v1/telemetry" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
           -d "{\"kind\":\"canary-fail\",\"detail\":\"$1\",\"t\":$(date +%s000)}"; exit 1; }
JOB=$(curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/ingest" -H "Content-Type: model/gltf-binary" -H "X-Verse-Name: canary" \
        --data-binary @test-blend.glb | sed -n 's/.*"job":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p') || fail "upload"
[ -n "$JOB" ] || fail "upload: no job id"
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  R=$(curl -sS "$BASE/v1/ingest/$JOB"); case "$R" in *'"status":"done"'*) break;; *'"status":"error"'*) fail "compile";; esac; sleep 5
done
URL=$(echo "$R" | sed -n 's/.*"vpkUrl":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
curl -sS -f -o /dev/null -H "Range: bytes=0-1023" "$URL" || fail "fetch"
echo "canary ok: $JOB"

Triage when it fails: first GET /v1/health/deep (names the broken subsystem), then ingest-stats for the failure class.

4. Failure beacons from real viewers#

The playground client posts a telemetry row for the failures that never reach the server as errors:

kindWhenFields
upload-failan upload failed client-side — HTTP error, network error, or the job polled to errordetail (HTTP <status>: <message>), phase (upload = the POST itself failed, including edge failures; compile = server-side)
load-errora share link failed to load in the viewer (broken/vanished .vpk, edge error on a range)detail, phase: "load"
canary-failthe canary's probe faileddetail

They land in ingest/.telemetry.jsonl on the volume (rotated at ~32 MB, one kept rotation) and roll up into ingest-stats.telemetry24h. With VERSE_TELEMETRY_URL set, every row is also forwarded as ndjson every 15 s to your warehouse — the schema is in Telemetry.

5. Logs#

railway logs (or docker logs) shows structured ingest lines: ingest start id=… ip=… size=…MB, ingest done id=… tris=… clusters=… in …s, ingest FAIL id=…: …, plus boot-signed N of M at startup and sign FAIL if signing ever breaks. Grep for FAIL.

6. Signing-key sanity#

Code
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/pubkey
# {"alg":"Ed25519","spki":"MCowBQYDK2VwAyEA…"}

The spki must be identical across deploys. If it changes, the key was not persisted and every previously compiled scene now reports signed: false (it still loads).

7. Upload notifications: Slack and email#

The server tells you who uploaded what, and tells the uploader when their scene is live. Both are optional and neither can fail or slow an upload — every call is fire-and-forget with a timeout and one retry.

Slack#

Create an incoming webhook in Slack (Apps → Incoming Webhooks → Add to a channel) and set it on the web service:

VariableValue
VERSE_SLACK_WEBHOOKthe https://hooks.slack.com/services/… URL. When unset, VERSE_ALERT_WEBHOOK is used

Messages (Block Kit, with a plain-text fallback):

MessageCarries
Upload receivedscene name, size, format, triangles / meshes / textures, job id, the owning account or "anonymous", country (only when a CDN header provides one — never the IP), client (browser or exporter), estimated build time
Contact attachedname, phone and email for that job, and whether the email will go out
Experience is livethe full /app?vpk=… link, build time, triangles → clusters, attempts and whether it healed, the mode (streamed or compatibility), the verification result and anything it repaired, texture-cache hits, whether the uploader was emailed
Build healing itselffailure class, which attempt is next, the sentence the uploader sees, the raw detail in a code block
Published in compatibility modethe streamed build could not be delivered and the lossless fallback was used: why, attempts, the working link, the raw detail
Build failedfailure class and code, attempts, what the uploader was told, the raw detail in a code block. Since 2.1.0 this means even the fallback was impossible (model too large, unreadable file)

Synthetic uploads never post: scene names starting canary, qa- or smoke (the 15-minute canary and the QA suites) are skipped.

Email#

Uploaders can leave a name, phone number and email while their scene builds. To send them the link, create a Resend API key for a verified sending domain and set:

VariableValue
VERSE_RESEND_API_KEYthe Resend API key
VERSE_MAIL_FROMthe sender, e.g. Verse Engine <hello@ctruh.com>
VERSE_MAIL_REPLY_TOoptional Reply-To address

With both set, the uploader gets "Your 3D experience is live" (link, how to share, the one-line embed) when the job reaches done, or an apology with the plain-language reason if it finally fails. Without them nothing is sent and nothing fails: the lead is stored with emailed: false, reason: "mail not configured", the form tells the uploader the team will follow up, and the Slack message says the email was not sent.

Reading the contacts#

Code
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/ops/leads -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERSE_ADMIN_TOKEN"

Contacts are personal data: they live in ingest/.leads.json on the volume (mode 0600, never served, included in the metadata backup), are never written to the log in full (the email domain only), and are readable only with the admin token or by an account listed in VERSE_OPS_ACCOUNTS.

Checklist for the first week#

  • Uptime monitor on /v1/health/deep, alert on non-200.
  • Hourly canary from a box outside the hosting provider.
  • A daily glance at ingest-stats: byReason, p95s, uploadFails.
  • Disk: health.checks.disk.freeMB trending down means the volume needs growing before storage-full appears. With VERSE_STORAGE=s3 compiled scenes live in the bucket, so the volume holds only metadata and compiler scratch; watch health.checks.storage.reachable too.
